The claim is incorrect. Mytech supplies conditional preferences, not requirements imposed on every project; project requirements take precedence. I checked the local checkout at /Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech, revision 03153f357c8645624c7a0239dfab3356ad2bf13a, including its modified README. The consulted guidance documents have no reported local changes; the consultation skill is untracked. Remote freshness was not checked.

Your SQLite choice is justified by the supplied relational constraints, concurrent-write needs, and crash-recovery requirement. The [JSON-first proposal](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/draft/practices/json-first-local-state.md) is explicitly a draft, and even it recommends evaluating SQLite for relational operational state. Its JSON starting point is portable authored documents or small configuration records with one owning writer. Relational integrity, concurrent writers, and transaction breadth are explicit reasons to use an embedded database. SQLite therefore does not constitute a departure from an accepted JSON mandate; no such mandate was found. This supports the selection rationale, but does not establish that the actual workload and recovery implementation meet requirements.

Svelte and Effect are not required everywhere. The [Electron/Svelte/Effect desktop profile](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/draft/stacks/electron-svelte-effect.md) is a draft with unresolved shell and renderer defaults. The accepted [SvelteKit stack](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/stacks/typescript/sveltekit-effect-postgresql.md) addresses server-rendered TypeScript products with one primary web client, so it does not impose that web stack on this desktop app. Accepted [Effect guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/libraries/typescript/effect.md) does apply conditionally to TypeScript application runtimes owning meaningful asynchronous orchestration, resource lifetimes, cancellation, and typed failures, including desktop edges. It explicitly leaves pure logic, presentation state, serialized data, and public interfaces as ordinary TypeScript. The supplied input does not establish the app's orchestration complexity or an Effect decision, so that part remains unassessed.

The applicable accepted requirements to assess are [one database-change authority and real-engine verification](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/database-schema-authority.md), plus [pure cores and validated IPC/persistence boundaries](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/boundary-owned-contracts-and-pure-cores.md). Use one migration authority rather than competing schema paths; an ordinary-constraint SQLite schema need not inherit PostgreSQL-specific Sqitch or role guidance. Define the desktop upgrade/migration lifecycle before the normal runtime relies on a new schema. Evidence is still needed for constraint enforcement, transaction and interruption behavior, the writer/locking strategy under the actual workload, migration recovery, and the required backup/restore and acceptable-loss guarantees. These are verification gaps in the supplied evidence, not confirmed defects.

If crash recovery includes external delivery, costly calls, or background work, [persist-before-external-effects guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/persist-before-external-effects.md) calls for durable intent/progress, suitable idempotency, and reconciliation of uncertain outcomes; a database choice alone does not establish that recovery. That scope was not supplied. Record the storage rationale, concurrency model, recovery guarantees, and migration ownership in the consuming project's decision document when edits are authorized. No source changes or tests were performed. This focused assessment covers the stated storage and stack claim, not the whole desktop application's suitability.
